L'eau ne tourne pas dans l'autre sens da: Water does not swirl the other way in Southern Hemisphere sinks: at that scale, the Coriolis force is far too weak compared with the shape of the basin and the eddies. At MIT in 1962, Ascher Shapiro had to let the water in a 2 m wide tank settle for 24 hours to measure it.

Les saisons ne viennent pas de la distan: The seasons don't come from the distance to the Sun: the Earth is closest to it in early January, in the middle of the Northern Hemisphere's winter. It is the tilt of its axis that changes the height of the Sun and the length of the day.

Le carbone, l'oxygène et le fer de notre: The carbon, oxygen and iron in our bodies were made in stars. The mechanism was described in 1957 in a paper that became famous under its four authors' initials: B²FH.
Maîtriser les galaxies et le Big Bang. L: Master galaxies and the Big Bang. The name, for its part, was a jibe.
Fred Hoyle, qui défendait un Univers éte: Fred Hoyle, who championed an eternal Universe, coined the expression “Big Bang” in March 1949 on BBC radio to describe the rival theory. People often hear mockery in it, which Hoyle always denied. The name stuck, and so did the theory.

Au temps de Colomb, les savants savaient: In Columbus's time, scholars knew the Earth was round; Eratosthenes had even measured it around 240 BC. Columbus was wrong about its size, which he thought much smaller. The myth of the medieval flat Earth comes mostly from the 19th century.

« Et pourtant elle tourne » : Galilée ne: “And yet it moves”: Galileo probably never murmured it before his judges in 1633. The phrase first appears in 1757, in a book by Giuseppe Baretti, more than a century after the trial.

On dit que les étoiles que l'on voit son: It is said that the stars we see may have died long ago. Almost all those visible to the naked eye are less than a few thousand light-years away, and live for millions or billions of years. Their light is late, not their death certificate.

La NASA aurait dépensé des millions pour: NASA supposedly spent millions on a pen that writes in space, while the Soviets used a pencil. False: Paul Fisher developed it at his own expense, and both agencies bought it, for a few dollars apiece. Pencils were a problem: the lead breaks and graphite dust conducts electricity.

Les premières exoplanètes confirmées, en: The first confirmed exoplanets, in 1992, did not orbit a star like the Sun, but a pulsar, the collapsed core of a star that had exploded. Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail spotted them from irregularities in its pulses.

En 1933, Fritz Zwicky mesure les galaxie: In 1933, Fritz Zwicky measured the galaxies of the Coma cluster: they moved too fast for the cluster to hold together. An invisible mass was needed, “dunkle Materie.” No one followed him for forty years. He reportedly called his colleagues “spherical bastards”: bastards whichever way you looked at them.

En 1781, William Herschel, musicien deve: In 1781, William Herschel, a musician turned astronomer, discovered a new planet, the first since antiquity. He wanted to call it “Georgium Sidus,” George's star, in honor of King George III, who paid him a pension. Astronomers preferred Uranus.
